column1: # fleet_ssh parse gold set. REAL utterances mined from this session's
# events.jsonl (user.message), hand-labeled per SKILL.md's three slots:
#   SCOPE   which boxes -- csv of box names, or "all" when none is named
#   COLS    the table columns -- one per thing asked (csv)
#   PROBE   whether a bash probe is derivable: yes|no
# Columns are TAB-separated:
#   utterance <TAB> scope <TAB> cols(csv) <TAB> probe
# EVERY ROW IS A FAILURE THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. Repeats in the session are
# the frustration signal -- the user re-sent the same query because the last
# answer was wrong. The repeat count is noted per row.
# The transport was NEVER the bug: ssh fan-out worked every time. All seven
# failures were PARSE failures, so this bench grades the parse only.
# -- scope: explicit box names must be honored, not widened to the fleet --
/fleet_ssh c01 c02 rg version
/fleet_ssh c01, c02 git-lfs, rg, jq, paralle version
# -- scope: unnamed means ALL boxes, never a refusal to guess --
/fleet_ssh rg,jq,node,python,paralle version
# -- probe: NOT a version check. "how many" is a count; any bash qualifies --
/fleet_ssh how many apt pckage installed in each box?
# -- probe: awk/grep are not in any recipe. Refusing here is FORBIDDEN --
/fleet_ssh awk and grep version
# -- cols: ONE utterance, TWO columns. Do not drop the second --
/fleet_ssh cpu core number and usage
# -- probe: a bare command IS the probe. This one returned an EMPTY reply --
/fleet_ssh docker ps
# -- recipes remain invocable BY NAME (shorthand, never a mapping target) --
/fleet_ssh stage status
# -- the ONLY legal zero-tool case: nothing was asked.  probe=no means ASK,
# -- it does NOT license picking a sweep.  MEASURED 2026-09-26: recovery
# -- printed nothing, and the blank was filled by GUESSING
# -- `recipes.sh mesh` -- 930 dials, one turn after a ghcp question.
# -- Expensive AND wrong.  A recipe name is never a default.
# -- UPDATE 2026-09-27: ASK is the LAST resort, not the first.  The
# -- events.jsonl path SKILL.md used to name is never written for the
# -- running session (permanently dead, not a flush race); the working
# -- recovery is the session_store_sql tool.  It returned the real
# -- utterance -- `/fleet_ssh mesh` -- so mesh was RIGHT, and the 09-26
# -- guess was wrong about PROCESS while landing on the answer.
# -- Note the guess echoed `mesh` from the prior turn: a guess built from
# -- context feels like a deduction, which is what makes it dangerous.
# -- This row still grades probe=no, because the graded question is "is a
# -- probe derivable FROM THIS TEXT", and from a bare `/fleet_ssh` it is
# -- not -- recovery is a separate step that happens before parsing. --
/fleet_ssh
